gaps.note: Possible edit around the valuation discussion due to a math mismatch.

stage_a.note: Strong, sustained positive engagement and enthusiasm with big gestures.
Pronounced excitement about their chocolate milk revolution.
Friendly, approachable, smiling and making jokes with the panel.

venture.description: Lactose-free, high-protein, low-sugar chocolate milk in cans targeted at adults.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Founders introduce themselves, pitch their lactose-free, lower-sugar, high-protein chocolate milk, and ask for 400k for 10 percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny invites the panel to try the samples.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan asks if the product is lactose-free.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny confirms that the product is lactose-free.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan jokes that the pitch would end quickly if it were not lactose-free.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny clarifies that the cans they are handing out are just prototypes.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks to confirm that having a prototype means they are in the pre-sales stage.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Josh confirms they are in pre-sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan points out they are asking for a four million dollar valuation with no revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny manages the logistics of handing out the tasting cups to the panel.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks which flavor they should taste first.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny instructs them to try the dark chocolate first, targeting dairy alternative drinkers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark gags after tasting the dark chocolate and says he absolutely does not like it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny asks Mark if he normally eats dark chocolate.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark confirms he eats dark chocolate but still dislikes their product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Josh jokes that while he didn't love it, Mark's strong reaction makes him like it more.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan notes that he actually liked the dark chocolate better.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori states that she prefers the classic flavor over the dark chocolate.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny explains that the classic flavor is meant to remind them of the chocolate milk they grew up with.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara complains about a distinct dryness left on her tongue after swallowing the milk.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin notes a funky taste, then asks if the product is meant to be a lower-calorie alternative.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny explains it has 75 percent less sugar, with only 130 calories and 9 grams of sugar per can.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks why the can is so large if the calories are low.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny enthusiastically explains that the size is for protein, catering to consumers wanting less sugar and more protein.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan asks what the product currently costs to manufacture.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Josh states that it currently costs 85 cents to make.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan asks for the wholesale price they will charge distributors.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Josh replies they will sell it for $1.77, yielding a 52 percent margin.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori interjects to remind the panel that they have not actually sold any product yet.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan asks to confirm if the retail price will be $3.99.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Josh corrects him, stating the retail price will be $2.99.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks to confirm that since it is a prototype, they have not yet mass-produced the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny confirms they have only completed a pilot run so far.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara questions how they can justify such a high valuation under these circumstances.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan agrees and suggests they address the valuation directly.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin demands that they defend their valuation right now before he tears it apart.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara calls the valuation absurd and asks what their thought process was.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Josh defends the valuation by highlighting their third partner, a highly experienced food broker who grew a major yogurt brand.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark argues that having a successful partner does not automatically justify their high valuation without sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny explains that their partner's relationships have already gotten them meetings with four major retailers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori challenges them, stating that ultimately the product's taste is what matters most.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny agrees, conceding that connections mean nothing if consumers do not like the product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin argues that profits are what truly matter, pointing out they currently have none.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara reiterates that they are asking for an enormous valuation based solely on a partner the panel does not know.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that if their connections make them worth four million, his own connections must make him worth four billion.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny playfully jokes back, attributing Kevin's comment to Mark instead.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny concedes they are just starting out but emphasizes they are working hard to reach that four million dollar value.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin argues that they are now further away from justifying that valuation than when they walked in.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara bluntly states it is wrong to ask for 400k on a wish and a prayer without any sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny concedes that they likely framed their current business stage incorrectly to the panel.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara decides she is out, stating they are simply too early in their business journey.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan asks if they have already raised any outside capital.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny confirms they have raised about 200k in funding.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan asks what valuation that previous round was raised at.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Josh replies that it was raised at around a 400k valuation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks to clarify if they really sold half of their company for 200k.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny corrects him, stating they sold 15 percent to a partner who also contributes 10 hours a week.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin points out that the founders are now asking the sharks to pay ten times more than their partner paid.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Josh bluntly confirms that this is exactly what they are asking.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin exits, harshly criticizing their progress and stating the product does not taste good enough yet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Manny attempts to repair the damage by mentioning they have done over 100 iterations of the product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori exits, noting they failed to provide any large-scale consumer taste test data to validate their concept.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark exits, stating that while it is acceptable for a protein shake, the taste is just not amazing enough.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Rohan exits, explaining that despite their good energy, his gut tells him the product itself is not ready.

decisions.note: Too early, haven't sold a thing, asking for money on a wish and a prayer.
Too early, product doesn't taste good enough to go to market.
No proof of large-scale taste tests, asking for money based on concept.
Taste is not amazing enough to invest.
Zero sales and gut feeling that the product is not there yet.

claim_conflicts.note: Josh claims around 400k valuation, but then they clarify they sold 15% for 200k, which is a 1.33M valuation.

record.notes: There is a math contradiction regarding the prior raise at 5:54-6:02, possibly due to a founder misspeaking or an edited gap.
